name: hammurabi-alehouse-laws
description: Babylonian statutes fixed what alehouse keepers could charge for beer and set penalties for short measures.

name: mesopotamian-glaze-cipher
description: A Mesopotamian scribe disguised the cuneiform spellings in a pottery glaze formula, the earliest known cipher.

name: nine-mens-morris-game
description: Players scratched Nine Men's Morris grids into temple stone in Egypt, moving pieces to form rows of three.

name: sphinx-cleared-from-sand
description: A young Egyptian prince dug the Great Sphinx of Giza out of the drifted desert sand and recorded the deed on a stele.

name: cowrie-shell-money-china
description: Shang dynasty China used cowrie shells as a standard medium of exchange, among the earliest currencies known.

name: turin-papyrus-map
description: Egyptian scribes drew the quarry roads and rock types of Wadi Hammamat, the oldest surviving geological map.

name: aegean-sponge-divers
description: Greek islanders dived on a single breath, weighted by a flat stone, to cut sponges free of the seabed.

name: mancala-sowing-game
description: Rows of shallow pits cut into stone across Africa and the Near East mark the sowing game family called mancala.

name: yan-shi-mechanical-man
description: Chinese texts credit the artificer Yan Shi with presenting King Mu of Zhou a life-size singing automaton.

name: babylonian-hour-division
description: Babylonian astronomers applied their base-sixty numbering to time, splitting the hour into sixty minutes and each minute again.

name: gulf-pearl-diving
description: Divers worked the oyster beds off Bahrain on held breath, feeding a pearl trade that reached Assyria and India.

name: hezekiah-tunnel-jerusalem
description: Judean workers cut a winding water tunnel through bedrock beneath Jerusalem, digging from both ends until they met.

name: terracotta-oil-lamp
description: Cheap wheel-thrown clay lamps burning olive oil became the common household light around the Mediterranean.

name: sennacherib-assassinated
description: The Assyrian king who besieged Jerusalem was killed by his own sons in a dispute over the succession.

name: temple-scroll-found-josiah
description: Workmen repairing the Temple in Jerusalem turned up a forgotten scroll of law, and King Josiah tore his robes and reformed the kingdom.

name: atbash-cipher-scribes
description: Hebrew scribes swapped each letter for its opposite in the alphabet, veiling Babylon's name inside prophecy.

name: babylonian-world-map
description: A clay tablet showed Babylon at the centre of a disc-shaped earth ringed by a bitter river and distant islands.

name: greek-symposium-wine
description: Greek men drank wine mixed with water from a shared krater, pairing poetry and music with measured drinking.

name: anaximander-earth-in-space
description: The Milesian philosopher argued Earth hangs unsupported in space, resting on nothing at all.

name: nabonidus-excavates-ur
description: The last king of Babylon dug beneath a ruined temple to recover its founder's buried inscription, an early act of archaeology.

name: histiaeus-tattooed-message
description: Histiaeus tattooed a call to revolt on a slave's shaved head and let the hair regrow, hiding it from Persian eyes.

name: scyllis-combat-diver
description: Herodotus recorded a Greek diver slipping among the Persian fleet at Artemisium to cut its ships adrift in a gale.

name: xerxes-hellespont-bridge
description: Persian engineers lashed hundreds of ships into twin pontoon bridges so an invading army could march into Europe.

name: sparta-earthquake
description: A violent quake levelled Sparta and killed thousands, touching off a helot revolt that nearly broke the city-state.

name: irrational-numbers-discovered
description: Pythagoreans found that the square root of two cannot be written as a ratio of two whole numbers.

name: metonic-cycle
description: Athenian astronomer Meton showed that nineteen solar years almost exactly equal two hundred and thirty-five lunar months.

name: syracuse-underwater-palisade
description: Athenian divers sawed through the piles Syracuse had sunk across its harbour mouth to trap the besieging fleet.

name: spartan-scytale-cipher
description: Spartan commanders wound a leather strip around a rod, so a dispatch could be read only on a rod of equal thickness.

name: punch-marked-coins-india
description: Mahajanapada kingdoms of northern India struck silver punch-marked coins, the subcontinent's first currency.

name: helike-earthquake
description: An earthquake and tsunami sank the Greek city of Helike into the Gulf of Corinth overnight, leaving nothing above water.

name: aeneas-tacticus-secret-messages
description: A Greek general's siege manual catalogued ways to smuggle word past a blockade, from pricked books to hollow soles.

name: archytas-flying-dove
description: The Greek mathematician Archytas of Tarentum built a wooden bird said to fly on its own using compressed air.

name: aristotle-celestial-spheres
description: Aristotle placed a motionless Earth inside nested crystalline spheres carrying the planets and stars.

name: aristotle-diving-kettle
description: Aristotle described divers drawing breath from an upturned cauldron lowered with them, the first account of a diving bell.

name: philip-ii-macedon-assassinated
description: The Macedonian king was struck down by one of his bodyguards at a royal wedding, bringing Alexander to the throne.

name: alexander-diving-bell
description: Legend held that Alexander the Great was lowered beneath the sea at Tyre in a glass barrel to watch the fish.

name: alexander-coinage-empire
description: Alexander the Great's silver tetradrachms carried one coin standard from Greece to the Indus, outlasting him.

name: archimedes-measures-circle
description: Archimedes squeezed the circle between inscribed and circumscribed polygons to pin down pi.

name: ctesibius-float-regulator
description: Ctesibius of Alexandria gave his water clock a float valve that held the supply level steady, an early feedback control.

name: rhodes-earthquake-colossus
description: A quake shattered the Colossus of Rhodes at the knees, and the fallen bronze wonder was left lying where it broke.

name: mawangdui-silk-maps
description: Maps painted on silk and buried in a Han noble's tomb showed rivers, garrisons and roads drawn close to scale.

name: confucian-classics-found-in-wall
description: Texts hidden from the Qin book burnings were recovered from a wall of Confucius' old house at Qufu, in a script scholars could barely read.

name: polybius-square-cipher
description: The Greek historian Polybius set the alphabet in a five-by-five grid so any letter became a pair of torch signals.

name: nine-chapters-mathematical-art
description: The Chinese classic set out problems using negative numbers and elimination on systems of equations.

name: roman-urinatores
description: The urinatores, a guild of Roman divers, recovered sunken cargo and dropped goods from the Tiber and the port of Ostia.

name: caesar-rhine-bridge
description: Roman legions drove piles into the riverbed and spanned the Rhine with a timber trestle bridge in ten days.

name: caesar-shift-cipher
description: Julius Caesar shifted every letter three places down the alphabet to keep his military dispatches from enemy hands.

name: julian-calendar-reform
description: Julius Caesar scrapped Rome's drifting lunar calendar for a solar year of three hundred sixty-five days plus a leap day.

name: caligula-assassinated
description: Officers of the Praetorian Guard killed the Roman emperor in his palace and raised Claudius in his place.

name: roman-factory-lamps
description: Italian potteries mass-produced mould-made oil lamps signed with maker's marks and shipped them across the empire.

name: trajans-bridge-danube
description: Apollodorus of Damascus spanned the Danube on stone piers with timber arches, the longest arch bridge for a millennium.

name: ptolemy-geographia
description: Ptolemy set out coordinates for thousands of places and rules for projecting a round earth onto a flat sheet.

name: commodus-assassinated
description: Members of his own household killed the Roman emperor, ending the Antonine line and opening a scramble for power.

name: ama-divers-japan
description: Chinese chronicles described Japanese women diving for shellfish and pearls, a breath-hold trade still practised today.

name: ma-jun-south-pointing-chariot
description: Ma Jun built a geared cart whose figure kept pointing south however the vehicle turned, using no magnet at all.

name: pei-xiu-map-principles
description: The Chinese minister Pei Xiu set out six rules for mapmaking, among them scale, grid and measured distance.

name: bamboo-annals-recovered
description: Robbers broke into a Warring States tomb at Ji and scattered a lost court chronicle written on bamboo strips, which scholars reassembled.

name: kamasutra-secret-writing
description: The Kama Sutra listed mlecchita vikalpa, the art of secret writing, among the sixty-four skills a cultured person learned.

name: san-marino-founded
description: A stonemason fleeing persecution settled Monte Titano, founding what became Europe's oldest surviving republic.

name: golgotha-excavated
description: Constantine's builders tore down a Roman temple in Jerusalem and dug out the rock-cut tomb venerated as the burial place of Christ.

name: peutinger-road-map
description: A scroll map squeezed the Roman road network into a long strip, listing way stations and the distances between them.

name: hypatia-of-alexandria-killed
description: The mathematician and philosopher was killed by a mob during a struggle for control of the city.

name: dionysius-anno-domini
description: The monk Dionysius Exiguus built an Easter table numbering years from the presumed birth of Christ, creating the AD era.

name: madaba-mosaic-map
description: A church floor mosaic in Jordan laid out the Holy Land and its towns, with the oldest surviving plan of Jerusalem.

name: anji-bridge-china
description: Li Chun built the oldest surviving open-spandrel segmental arch bridge, carrying a road over the Xiao River.

name: lantern-festival-sui
description: Emperor Yang staged vast lantern displays in the Sui capital, fixing the festival of lights in Chinese custom.

name: quran-forbids-wine
description: Revelation recorded in the Quran barred intoxicants for Muslims, reshaping what was drunk across the Islamic world.

name: hijri-calendar-adopted
description: Caliph Umar fixed the Muslim lunar calendar to count from Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina.

name: shatranj-persia
description: Persia reworked the Indian army game as shatranj, added written problem studies, and passed chess to the Arab world.

name: first-bulgarian-empire-founded
description: Khan Asparuh's Bulgars beat the Byzantines and won a treaty recognising their state south of the Danube.

name: japan-smallpox-epidemic
description: A smallpox epidemic carried in through Kyushu killed roughly a third of Japan's population.

name: lu-yu-classic-of-tea
friendly_name: Lu Yu Writes the Classic of Tea
description: Tang scholar Lu Yu compiled the first treatise on growing, brewing and drinking tea, codifying Chinese tea culture.

name: offas-dyke-built
description: Offa of Mercia, the most powerful ruler in England, raised a great earthwork rampart along the Welsh border.

name: mamun-opens-great-pyramid
description: Caliph al-Ma'mun's workmen hammered a tunnel through solid masonry into the sealed pyramid of Khufu, hunting for treasure.

name: al-kindi-frequency-analysis
description: The Baghdad scholar al-Kindi showed that counting how often each letter appears will break any simple substitution cipher.

name: banu-musa-ingenious-devices
description: The Banu Musa brothers of Baghdad catalogued a hundred self-acting devices, among them a flute player driven by a pinned cylinder.

name: candle-clock-alfred
description: King Alfred burned graduated wax candles inside horn lanterns to keep the hours and shield the flame from draughts.

name: al-battani-solar-year
description: The Syrian astronomer remeasured the length of the year and showed that the Sun's apogee slowly shifts.

name: tomislav-crowned-croatia
description: Tomislav drew the Croatian duchies together and is remembered as the first king of a Croatian kingdom.

name: athelstan-first-king-of-england
description: Athelstan took York from the Vikings and received the submission of the other British rulers, uniting England under one crown.

name: gorm-the-old-unites-denmark
description: Gorm ruled a single Danish realm from Jelling, and Europe's oldest monarchy still traces its line to him.

name: baptism-of-poland-mieszko
description: Mieszko I accepted Christianity, binding the Piast realm to Latin Europe and founding the Polish state.

name: nikephoros-phokas-assassinated
description: The Byzantine emperor was killed in the palace by his nephew John Tzimiskes, who then took the throne.

name: aethelred-unready-becomes-king
description: Aethelred took the English throne as a boy after his half-brother's murder; renewed Viking raids defined his long reign.

name: stephen-first-king-hungary
description: Stephen took a crown sent by the pope, turning the Magyar tribal confederation into a Christian kingdom.

name: ibn-al-haytham-doubts-ptolemy
description: Ibn al-Haytham catalogued the physical impossibilities in Ptolemy's cosmos, opening a long era of reform.

name: edward-confessor-becomes-king
description: The pious son of Aethelred returned from Norman exile to take the English throne, and went on to found Westminster Abbey.

name: luoyang-bridge-quanzhou
description: Cai Xiang's long stone beam bridge crossed a Fujian estuary on foundations that farmed oysters cemented together.

name: justinian-digest-rediscovered
description: A forgotten manuscript of Roman law resurfaced in Italy and became the founding text of European legal scholarship at Bologna.

name: kingdom-of-bohemia-established
description: Vratislav II was crowned the first king of Bohemia, the state at the root of the modern Czech lands.

name: nizam-al-mulk-assassinated
description: The Seljuk vizier was killed by an agent of the Nizari Ismailis, the sect that gave English the word assassin.

name: su-song-clock-tower
description: The Chinese official Su Song raised a water-driven clock tower whose puppet figures struck bells and drums each hour.

name: henry-i-charter-of-liberties
description: Henry I seized the throne on his brother's death and issued a coronation charter curbing royal abuses, a model for Magna Carta.

name: kaifeng-night-markets
description: Lamp-lit stalls kept the Song capital trading long past dusk, breaking the curfew that had closed Chinese cities at dark.

name: yu-ji-tu-grid-map
friendly_name: Yu Ji Tu Map Carved in Stone
description: Song engravers cut a map of China into stone over a square grid, its coastline and rivers strikingly accurate.

name: portugal-becomes-a-kingdom
description: Afonso Henriques won recognition from Leon as king, setting Portugal apart as a kingdom of its own.

name: henry-ii-becomes-king
description: Henry II ended the Anarchy and took the English throne, founding the Plantagenet line and an empire reaching to the Pyrenees.

name: privilegium-minus-austria
description: The Privilegium Minus raised the Babenberg march to a duchy of Austria with its own law and succession.

name: richard-lionheart-crowned
description: Richard I was crowned at Westminster and left within months for the Third Crusade, spending almost none of his reign in England.

name: serbian-kingdom-stefan-crowned
description: Stefan Nemanjic was crowned the first king of Serbia, uniting the Serbian lands under a single crown.

name: aqua-vitae-distilled
description: Italian physicians distilled wine into aqua vitae, the first spirit drunk in Europe as medicine and then for pleasure.

name: bacon-undersea-instruments
description: Roger Bacon wrote of instruments by which men might walk on the bed of the sea without danger to the body.

name: mindaugas-crowned-lithuania
description: Mindaugas bound the Lithuanian tribes into one realm and became the only crowned king Lithuania has had.

name: tusi-couple-planetary-model
description: The Maragha astronomer built straight-line motion out of two rotating circles, repairing Ptolemy's cosmos.

name: paris-candlemakers-guild
description: The provost's book of trades set statutes for the tallow and wax chandlers who supplied the city with light.

name: andorra-pareatges-signed
description: A bishop and a count settled their quarrel by sharing the valleys, creating the co-principality of Andorra.

name: alfonso-book-of-games
description: Alfonso the Wise of Castile had scribes compile an illustrated manuscript of chess, dice and tables games.

name: edward-i-annexes-wales
description: The Statute of Rhuddlan bound the Welsh principality to the English crown after Edward I crushed Llywelyn's rising.

name: hereford-mappa-mundi
description: The largest surviving medieval world map put Jerusalem at its centre and east at the top, mixing scripture with geography.

name: edward-ii-deposed
description: Parliament forced Edward II to give up the crown to his young son after years of misrule; he died in captivity soon after.

name: mamluk-mosque-lamps
description: Cairo glassmakers gilded and enamelled oil lamps that hung by the dozen in Mamluk mosques, prized far beyond Egypt.

name: sandglass-at-sea
description: European ships adopted the sandglass to time the crew's watches and, paired with a knotted line, to log a vessel's speed.

name: edward-iii-claims-french-crown
friendly_name: Edward III Claims the French Crown
description: Edward III formally styled himself King of France and quartered the French lilies with the English lions on his arms.

name: petrarch-finds-cicero-letters
description: In a cathedral library at Verona, Petrarch turned up Cicero's private correspondence and lit the fuse of Renaissance humanism.

name: ponte-vecchio-florence
description: Florence rebuilt its shop-lined stone bridge over the Arno after a flood swept the previous crossing away.

name: ibn-al-shatir-lunar-model
description: The Damascus timekeeper modelled the Moon and planets without Ptolemy's equant, geometry Copernicus later echoed.

name: strasbourg-clock-rooster
description: The cathedral clock carried a gilded cock that flapped its wings, opened its beak and crowed at midday.

name: basel-earthquake
description: The strongest quake known in central Europe destroyed Basel and threw down castles for miles along the Rhine.

name: charles-bridge-prague
description: Charles IV laid the first stone of a fortified bridge across the Vltava in Prague, replacing a flood-wrecked span.

name: principality-of-moldavia-founded
description: Bogdan I threw off Hungarian overlordship to found Moldavia, the state modern Moldova traces itself to.

name: catalan-atlas
description: A Majorcan workshop produced a lavish sea atlas showing Mansa Musa, the roads to Asia and a drawn compass rose.

name: playing-cards-reach-europe
description: A Swiss monk recorded the sudden arrival of playing cards, carried from Mamluk Egypt through Mediterranean ports.

name: wat-tyler-killed
description: The leader of the English peasants' rising was struck down at a parley with the king, breaking the revolt.

name: salisbury-cathedral-clock
description: The faceless wrought-iron clock at Salisbury began striking the hours, and still runs as one of the oldest of its kind.

name: kangnido-world-map
description: Korean scholars merged Chinese, Islamic and Japanese sources into a world map reaching as far as Africa and Europe.

name: louis-of-orleans-assassinated
description: The French king's brother was killed in Paris on the orders of the Duke of Burgundy, starting a long civil war.

name: prague-astronomical-clock
description: The Orloj was mounted on Prague's Old Town Hall, showing the hour, the zodiac and the positions of sun and moon.

name: london-lantern-order
description: The mayor required householders to hang lanterns outside on dark evenings, an early rule for lighting city streets.

name: poggio-recovers-lucretius
description: The book hunter Poggio Bracciolini found the last surviving copy of the Roman poem On the Nature of Things in a German abbey.

name: voynich-manuscript-created
description: An illustrated codex was written in an unknown script that has since defeated every professional codebreaker who tried it.

name: henry-vi-crowned-in-paris
description: The boy king of England was crowned King of France at Notre-Dame, the only monarch ever crowned in both kingdoms.

name: cusa-infinite-universe
description: Nicholas of Cusa argued the universe has no centre and no outer edge, and that stars are other suns.

name: alberti-cipher-disk
description: Leon Battista Alberti mounted two lettered discs that turned mid-message, the first cipher to switch alphabets as it ran.

name: printed-ptolemy-maps
description: A Bologna press issued the Geographia with engraved maps, putting identical copies of one world picture into many hands.

name: pazzi-conspiracy
description: Rival bankers attacked the Medici brothers during Mass in Florence. Giuliano was killed and Lorenzo escaped.

name: domus-aurea-rediscovered
description: Romans lowered themselves on ropes into buried painted halls under a hillside, and copied the decoration as the grotesque style.

name: first-scotch-whisky-record
description: Scotland's exchequer rolls logged malt granted to Friar John Cor to make aqua vitae, the earliest whisky record.

name: leonardo-mechanical-knight
description: Leonardo da Vinci designed an armoured figure worked by cables and pulleys that could sit, stand and move its arms.

name: meio-nankai-earthquake
description: A megathrust quake on Japan's Nankai Trough drove a tsunami that swept away the hall sheltering the Great Buddha of Kamakura.

name: leonardo-diving-apparatus
description: Leonardo da Vinci sketched a leather diving suit, webbed gloves and a breathing tube, withholding it for fear of use in war.

name: laocoon-unearthed
description: Diggers in a Roman vineyard struck an ancient marble group of a priest and his sons in the coils of serpents; Michelangelo came to look.

name: henlein-portable-watch
description: Nuremberg locksmith Peter Henlein built spring-driven clocks small enough to carry, ancestors of the pocket watch.

name: reinheitsgebot-beer-purity
description: Bavaria decreed that beer be brewed from barley, hops and water alone, a purity rule German brewers still cite.

name: trithemius-polygraphia
description: The abbot Trithemius left a printed manual whose square table enciphered each letter of a message with a fresh alphabet.

name: joachimsthaler-first-struck
description: Silver from the Bohemian valley of Joachimsthal was struck into big coins whose name became the word dollar.

name: gustav-vasa-elected-king
description: Gustav Vasa's election as king broke the Kalmar Union and set Sweden on its own course as a nation.

name: nemi-diving-bell
description: Guglielmo de Lorena descended in a bell resting on his shoulders to survey Caligula's sunken pleasure barges.

name: great-debasement-henry-viii
description: Henry VIII cut the silver out of English coins to fund his wars, and the crown's money lost most of its value.

name: cardano-ars-magna
description: Cardano printed general solutions to the cubic and quartic, and met square roots of negative numbers.

name: variolation-china
description: Ming physicians recorded blowing powdered smallpox scabs into the nose to induce mild, protective infection.

name: japanese-andon-lantern
description: Wooden frames screened with paper sheltered a rapeseed-oil wick, becoming the standard household lamp in Japan.

name: mary-i-becomes-queen
description: Mary Tudor took the throne as England's first ruling queen and set about restoring the Catholic faith by force.

name: turriano-mechanical-friar
description: Clockmaker Juanelo Turriano built a wind-up friar that walked a table top, beat its breast and kissed a rosary.

name: stari-most-mostar
description: Ottoman architect Mimar Hayruddin threw a single soaring stone arch across the Neretva gorge at Mostar.

name: murder-of-lord-darnley
description: The consort of Mary, Queen of Scots died when his Edinburgh lodging was destroyed, wrecking her hold on the throne.

name: tycho-new-star
description: A brilliant new star appeared among the fixed stars, proving the heavens beyond the Moon do change.

name: roman-catacombs-rediscovered
description: A collapse on the Via Salaria opened miles of forgotten Christian burial galleries beneath the Roman countryside.

name: gregorian-calendar-reform
description: Pope Gregory XIII struck ten days from the year and changed the leap rule to stop Easter drifting away from the equinox.

name: william-of-orange-assassinated
description: The leader of the Dutch revolt was shot at his house in Delft by a Catholic seeking a bounty offered by Spain.

name: babington-plot-cipher-broken
description: Elizabeth I's codebreaker deciphered letters in which Mary, Queen of Scots blessed a plot to assassinate the queen.

name: galileo-pendulum-isochronism
description: Galileo argued that a pendulum takes the same time to swing whatever the width of its arc, the principle behind exact clocks.

name: ricci-chinese-world-map
description: Matteo Ricci and Chinese scholars printed a world map showing the Americas, with China set near the centre of the sheet.

name: pont-neuf-paris
description: Paris opened its first bridge built with no houses on it, giving the city clear views along the Seine.

name: henry-iv-france-assassinated
description: The king who ended the French wars of religion was stabbed by Francois Ravaillac in a Paris street.

name: cordouan-lighthouse
description: A royal tower crowned by an open fire rose at the mouth of the Gironde to guide ships past its shoals.

name: napier-logarithms
description: John Napier published tables turning multiplication into addition, transforming astronomical calculation.

name: drebbel-submarine-thames
description: Cornelis Drebbel rowed a greased leather boat beneath the Thames, the first navigable submarine ever demonstrated.

name: bacon-bilateral-cipher
description: Francis Bacon encoded each letter as a five-symbol group of two typefaces, concealing a message inside innocent text.

name: wallenstein-assassinated
description: The Habsburg emperor's leading general was killed by his own officers once he was suspected of treating with the enemy.

name: ridotto-venice-casino
description: Venice licensed the Ridotto, a public gaming house where masked patrons played card games under state supervision.

name: great-cipher-of-france
description: The Rossignols enciphered the correspondence of Louis XIV with hundreds of numbered syllables, resisting attack for centuries.

name: restoration-of-charles-ii
description: Charles II returned from exile to a cheering London, restoring the monarchy and ending Puritan rule in England.

name: blaeu-atlas-maior
description: Joan Blaeu published a multi-volume Amsterdam atlas of hundreds of hand-coloured maps, the costliest book of its age.

name: first-colonial-rum-distillery
description: A Staten Island distillery began turning Caribbean molasses into rum, seeding a trade that fuelled Atlantic commerce.

name: vasa-cannon-salvaged
description: Divers working from a lead bell hauled dozens of bronze guns off a Swedish warship lying deep in Stockholm harbour.

name: paris-street-lanterns
description: Police chief La Reynie strung candle lanterns above the streets, and the capital earned its name as the city of light.

name: etna-catania-eruption
description: Mount Etna's largest recorded eruption pushed lava through the walls of Catania and on into the sea, reshaping Sicily's coast.

name: balance-spring-watch
description: Christiaan Huygens fitted a spiral spring to a watch balance wheel, making portable timepieces vastly more accurate.

name: canal-du-midi-opens
description: Pierre-Paul Riquet's canal joined the Atlantic to the Mediterranean and bored the first tunnel cut for shipping.

name: halley-diving-bell
description: Edmond Halley kept divers down for hours by sending weighted barrels of fresh air to a bell sunk in the Thames.

name: dominoes-reach-europe
description: Chinese tile games arrived in Italy and France as dominoes, sets of pip-marked bones matched end to end.

name: queen-anne-accession
description: The last Stuart monarch took the throne; England and Scotland were joined into a single kingdom during her reign.

name: herculaneum-well-discovery
description: Workmen sinking a well near Naples hit the marble seats of a Roman theatre buried under volcanic rock.

name: george-i-hanoverian-succession
description: The German-speaking Elector of Hanover became George I of Great Britain, passing over dozens of nearer Catholic claimants.

name: longitude-act
description: Parliament offered a fortune to anyone who could fix a ship's longitude at sea, a problem that came down to keeping time.

name: lethbridge-diving-engine
description: John Lethbridge sealed himself into an oak barrel with leather armholes and stripped wrecks for the East India Company.

name: vienna-black-chamber
description: Habsburg clerks opened, copied and resealed foreign diplomatic mail each morning, sending the decrypts on to the emperor.

name: liechtenstein-principality-created
description: The emperor merged Schellenberg and Vaduz into one imperial principality named for the family that bought them.

name: marseille-plague
description: A plague ship from the Levant loosed the last major bubonic plague epidemic in western Europe.

name: vaucanson-digesting-duck
description: Jacques de Vaucanson exhibited a gilded copper duck that flapped, swallowed grain and appeared to digest it.

name: cassini-map-of-france
description: The Cassini family triangulated France, yielding the first national map built from measured angles rather than report.

name: spermaceti-candle-works
description: Rhode Island refiners pressed whale head oil into hard candles that burned bright and smokeless, setting the standard.

name: kant-island-universes
description: Kant argued the faint nebulae are whole systems of stars like the Milky Way, each an island universe.

name: guinness-brewery-lease
description: Arthur Guinness signed a nine-thousand-year lease on a disused Dublin brewery and began brewing porter there.

name: george-iii-becomes-king
description: George III took the throne as the first Hanoverian born in Britain; his long reign saw America lost and Napoleon beaten.

name: peter-iii-of-russia-killed
description: The Russian emperor was deposed by guards loyal to his wife Catherine and died in custody days afterwards.

name: bayes-theorem
description: Thomas Bayes' posthumous essay showed how evidence should update the probability of a hypothesis.

name: mechanical-turk-chess-automaton
description: Wolfgang von Kempelen unveiled a chess-playing automaton at the Habsburg court, secretly steered by a hidden operator.

name: moscow-plague-riot
description: Plague deaths and harsh quarantines drove Muscovites to riot, killing the archbishop who sealed a shrine.

name: jaquet-droz-writer-automaton
description: Pierre Jaquet-Droz built a clockwork boy that dipped a quill and wrote any short text set on its cam wheel.

name: turtle-submarine-attack
description: David Bushnell's one-man submarine tried to screw a powder charge into a British flagship's hull in New York harbour.

name: argand-lamp
description: A tubular wick and a glass chimney fed air to the flame, giving Aime Argand's lamp the light of ten candles.

name: schweppes-bottled-soda-water
description: Johann Jacob Schweppe sold bottled carbonated water made by his own process in Geneva, launching the soft-drink trade.

name: herschel-milky-way-shape
description: By counting stars in every direction, William Herschel drew the first map of our galaxy's shape.

name: smeaton-diving-bell-pump
description: John Smeaton fed a cast-iron diving bell from a force pump on the surface, freeing divers from a fixed supply of air.

name: watt-centrifugal-governor
description: James Watt fitted spinning weights that throttled a steam engine to hold its speed steady with no attendant.

name: ordnance-survey-founded
description: Britain began mapping the whole country at one inch to the mile, working out from a measured baseline on Hounslow Heath.

name: french-republican-calendar
description: Revolutionary France replaced the week with ten-day decades and briefly ran a decimal clock of ten hours to the day.

name: marat-killed-by-corday
description: The radical journalist was killed at home by Charlotte Corday, who held him responsible for the Terror.

name: jefferson-wheel-cipher
description: Thomas Jefferson stacked twenty-six lettered discs on a spindle, devising one of the strongest ciphers of his day.

name: gauss-disquisitiones
description: Carl Friedrich Gauss systematised number theory, introducing modular arithmetic and congruences.

name: great-trigonometrical-survey
description: Surveyors began chaining a meridian arc across India, the measurement that later gave Himalayan peaks their heights.

name: pontcysyllte-aqueduct
description: Thomas Telford carried a canal high across the Dee valley in a cast iron trough resting on slender stone piers.

name: great-paris-cipher-broken
description: Wellington's officer George Scovell cracked the number cipher carrying Napoleon's orders across Spain, laying French plans bare.

name: petra-rediscovered
description: Disguised as a pilgrim, Johann Ludwig Burckhardt talked his way through a Jordanian gorge into the abandoned rock-cut city.

name: spencer-perceval-assassinated
description: A merchant with a grievance shot the prime minister in the lobby of the Commons, the only such killing in Britain.

name: baltimore-gas-streetlights
description: Baltimore laid coal-gas mains and became the first American city to light its streets with gas.

name: first-cholera-pandemic
description: Cholera spread out of the Ganges delta along trade and troop routes, beginning a century of global waves.

name: babbage-difference-engine
description: Charles Babbage began a geared machine meant to compute and print mathematical tables free of human error.

name: deane-diving-helmet
description: Brothers John and Charles Deane turned a firefighting smoke helmet into an open diving helmet fed by an air hose.

name: olbers-dark-night-sky
description: Olbers asked why the night is dark, when an endless and ageless universe of stars should blaze everywhere.

name: kriegsspiel-prussian-army
description: The Prussian army took up Kriegsspiel, a map-and-dice war game used to drill officers in tactical decisions.

name: american-temperance-society
description: Reformers in Boston founded a national society urging Americans to give up spirits, seeding the drive for prohibition.

name: non-euclidean-geometry
description: Lobachevsky described a consistent geometry in which parallel lines through a point are not unique.

name: jackson-assassination-attempt
description: Both pistols misfired when a house painter confronted the president at the Capitol, the first attempt on one in office.

name: brahmi-script-deciphered
description: James Prinsep cracked the script of Ashoka's pillar edicts, making India's oldest inscriptions readable and restoring a lost emperor.

name: siebe-closed-diving-dress
description: Augustus Siebe sealed a helmet to a watertight suit with an outlet valve, creating the standard diving dress.

name: victoria-becomes-queen
description: A teenage princess succeeded her uncle William IV, beginning a reign that would give its name to an age.

name: bessel-stellar-parallax
description: Bessel caught the tiny yearly wobble of the star 61 Cygni, yielding the first true distance to a star.

name: luxembourg-independence-london
description: A treaty in London partitioned the grand duchy, leaving a smaller Luxembourg as a sovereign state.

name: railway-time-britain
description: The Great Western Railway set every station clock to London time, overriding the patchwork of local solar times.

name: pilsner-first-brewed
description: Brewers in Plzen used pale malt and bottom-fermenting yeast to make a clear golden lager that reshaped world beer.

name: thames-tunnel-opens
description: Marc and Isambard Brunel finished the first tunnel driven under a navigable river, using a protective shield.

name: galois-group-theory
description: Liouville printed Evariste Galois' papers, whose groups explained why the general quintic has no formula.

name: nineveh-palace-excavated
description: Austen Henry Layard hauled winged bulls and carved battle reliefs out of the mounds of the buried Assyrian capital.

name: dover-calais-submarine-cable
description: An armoured cable laid across the Channel from Dover to Calais carried the first lasting telegraph traffic under the sea.

name: kerosene-lamp
description: Ignacy Lukasiewicz built a lamp burning distilled rock oil, a cheap bright fuel that soon displaced whale oil.

name: boole-laws-of-thought
description: George Boole recast logic as algebra on true and false, the calculus digital circuits would later use.

name: playfair-cipher-invented
description: Charles Wheatstone devised a cipher that scrambled letters in pairs on a small grid, and Britain took it to war.

name: snow-cholera-map
description: John Snow plotted cholera deaths as bars on a street plan, showing them clustered around a single water pump.

name: cuneiform-deciphered
description: Four scholars sealed their independent translations of the same Assyrian text; the versions matched, proving the wedge script could be read.

name: great-clock-westminster
description: The tower clock and its great bell, Big Ben, began keeping time above the Palace of Westminster in London.

name: kirchhoff-stellar-composition
description: Kirchhoff and Bunsen showed that dark lines in a spectrum name the elements, so the Sun could be read.

name: kingdom-of-italy-proclaimed
description: The first national parliament meeting in Turin proclaimed Victor Emmanuel II king of a united Italy.

name: us-greenbacks-issued
description: To fund the Civil War, Congress issued unbacked paper dollars nicknamed greenbacks and made them legal tender.

name: kasiski-vigenere-attack
description: The Prussian officer Friedrich Kasiski published a way to find a repeating key's length, ending faith in the Vigenère cipher.

name: hunley-sinks-housatonic
description: A hand-cranked Confederate submarine drove a spar torpedo into a Union sloop, then vanished with all hands aboard.

name: london-main-drainage
description: Bazalgette's intercepting sewers carried waste below the tideway, ending London's great cholera outbreaks.

name: whitehead-torpedo
description: Robert Whitehead's torpedo ran under its own power, held at a set depth by a concealed pendulum and valve.

name: challenger-expedition
description: A converted Royal Navy corvette set out to sound and dredge the world's oceans, founding the science of oceanography.

name: german-gold-mark-adopted
description: Paid a French war indemnity in gold, the new German Empire dropped silver for a gold mark and pulled Europe onto the gold standard.

name: cantor-uncountable-infinity
description: Georg Cantor showed the real numbers cannot be counted off, so some infinities are larger than others.

name: mahjong-emerges-china
description: Card games around Shanghai and Ningbo were remade in tile form as mahjong, drawing and discarding to build sets.

name: romania-independence-recognized
description: The great powers recognised Romania as a sovereign state after it fought the Ottomans alongside Russia.

name: altamira-paintings-found
description: A child looked up in a Spanish cave and saw a ceiling crowded with painted bison that her excavating father had walked beneath.

name: johnson-thermostat
description: Warren Johnson patented a thermostat that sensed room temperature and signalled a damper to open or close.

name: kerckhoffs-principle
description: Auguste Kerckhoffs argued a military cipher must stay safe even when the enemy knows the system, so only the key is secret.

name: first-world-chess-championship
description: Wilhelm Steinitz beat Johannes Zukertort in a match across three American cities to become world chess champion.

name: yersin-plague-bacillus
description: Alexandre Yersin isolated the bacterium behind bubonic plague during the Hong Kong epidemic.

name: niagara-falls-power
description: Generators at the falls sent alternating current to Buffalo, proving light could be made far from where it burns.

name: antikythera-wreck-found
description: Greek sponge divers sheltering from a gale found a Roman wreck holding bronzes, marbles and a geared bronze computer.

name: hilbert-problems
description: David Hilbert set out unsolved problems at the Paris congress, framing an agenda for mathematics.

name: knossos-palace-excavated
description: Arthur Evans uncovered a labyrinth of halls and frescoes on Crete and named their builders the Minoans.

name: mount-pelee-eruption
description: A pyroclastic flow from Mount Pelée obliterated Saint-Pierre on Martinique in minutes, killing almost every resident.

name: tungsten-filament-lamp
description: Hungarian chemists patented a bulb with a tungsten filament, brighter and far longer-lived than carbon threads.

name: haldane-decompression-tables
description: John Scott Haldane's tables of staged ascents let divers surface from depth without crippling nitrogen bubbles.

name: manchurian-plague
description: Pneumonic plague swept Manchuria until Wu Lien-teh's gauze masks and rail cordons broke the chain.

name: sperry-gyroscopic-autopilot
description: Lawrence Sperry linked gyroscopes to an aircraft's controls so the plane could hold its course unattended.

name: aerial-survey-photography
description: Cameras flown over the Western Front let armies redraw trench maps within hours, founding modern photographic survey.

name: daylight-saving-time
description: Germany pushed its clocks forward an hour to save coal, and rival and neutral nations copied the measure within weeks.

name: finland-declares-independence
description: The Finnish parliament declared the country independent of Russia as the Russian empire fell apart.

name: house-of-windsor-founded
description: George V renounced his family's German titles and renamed the royal house Windsor amid wartime anti-German feeling.

name: vernam-one-time-pad
description: Gilbert Vernam combined each teleprinter character with a key tape; with a random key used once, the result is unbreakable.

name: enigma-machine-sold
description: Arthur Scherbius marketed his rotor cipher machine to banks and firms before the German military adopted it wholesale.

name: pancho-villa-assassinated
description: The retired Mexican revolutionary general was ambushed by gunmen at Parral, three years after laying down arms.

name: contract-bridge-devised
description: Harold Vanderbilt reworked auction bridge on a Caribbean cruise, creating the bidding and scoring game played today.

name: godel-incompleteness-theorems
description: Kurt Godel proved that any consistent system rich enough for arithmetic holds truths it cannot prove.

name: rejewski-breaks-enigma
description: Marian Rejewski used permutation theory to reconstruct the wiring of the German army's Enigma without ever seeing one.

name: prohibition-repealed-us
description: The Twenty-first Amendment ended national prohibition, returning the regulation of alcohol to the American states.

name: bathysphere-descent
description: William Beebe and Otis Barton were winched half a mile down off Bermuda in a steel sphere, describing the life outside.

name: edward-viii-abdicates
description: Edward VIII gave up the throne to marry the divorcee Wallis Simpson, and his shy younger brother became George VI.

name: turing-computable-numbers
description: Alan Turing's paper on computable numbers described an abstract machine and problems no machine can settle.

name: zwicky-dark-matter
description: Galaxies in the Coma cluster moved far too fast for their visible mass, implying unseen matter holds them.

name: fluorescent-lamp
description: General Electric marketed phosphor-coated tubes that gave several times more light per watt than filament bulbs.

name: sutton-hoo-excavated
description: Basil Brown traced the vanished timbers of a ship in a Suffolk mound and found the gold and garnet regalia of an Anglo-Saxon king.

name: turing-bombe-bletchley
description: Alan Turing's electromechanical bombe began running at Bletchley Park, stripping out the German Enigma's daily settings.

name: aqua-lung-invented
description: Jacques Cousteau and Emile Gagnan's demand valve let a diver breathe compressed air at will, creating modern scuba.

name: colossus-lorenz-codebreaker
description: Bletchley Park's Colossus, the first programmable electronic computer, hunted the settings of Hitler's teleprinter cipher.

name: paricutin-volcano-born
description: A Mexican farmer watched a fissure split his field and grow into a cinder cone hundreds of feet tall, burying two villages.

name: iceland-becomes-republic
description: Icelanders voted to end the union with the Danish crown and founded their republic at Thingvellir.

name: gamow-hot-big-bang
description: Gamow argued the expanding universe began hot and dense enough to forge the lightest chemical elements.

name: espresso-machine-crema
description: Achille Gaggia's lever machine forced hot water through ground coffee under pressure, giving espresso its crema.

name: grey-walter-tortoises
description: Neurologist William Grey Walter built Elmer and Elsie, shelled robots that hunted light and recharged themselves.

name: shannon-perfect-secrecy
description: Claude Shannon put cryptography on a mathematical footing and proved the one-time pad the only theoretically unbreakable cipher.

name: linear-b-deciphered
description: Michael Ventris, an architect working in his spare time, showed that the Mycenaean tablet script recorded an early form of Greek.

name: mackinac-bridge
description: A five-mile suspension bridge joined Michigan's upper and lower peninsulas across the storm-swept Straits.

name: stellar-nucleosynthesis-b2fh
description: Burbidge, Fowler and Hoyle showed stars build nearly every heavy element and scatter them as they die.

name: tharp-ocean-floor-map
description: Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen turned sounding data into a picture of the Atlantic seabed, revealing a rift along its ridge.

name: mark-i-perceptron
description: Frank Rosenblatt's machine learned to tell shapes apart by adjusting its own weights, an early neural network.

name: samuel-checkers-program
description: Arthur Samuel's checkers program improved by playing against itself, an early demonstration of machine learning.

name: maya-glyphs-deciphered
description: Tatiana Proskouriakoff showed that Maya inscriptions record the births, accessions and wars of real kings, not only astronomy.

name: unimate-industrial-robot
description: The first industrial robot arm went to work unloading a die-casting machine at a General Motors plant.

name: cohen-continuum-hypothesis
description: Paul Cohen's forcing method showed the continuum hypothesis can be neither proved nor disproved from set theory.

name: malta-independence
description: Malta became independent from Britain, ending a long run of rule by outside powers over the islands.

name: si-second-caesium
description: Weights and measures delegates defined the second by caesium atom vibrations, untying it from the spin of the Earth.

name: shakey-the-robot
description: Stanford researchers built the first mobile robot able to plan its own route and reason about its actions.

name: crypto-ag-rigged-machines
description: American and West German spy agencies secretly bought a Swiss cipher firm and sold weakened machines to scores of governments.

name: low-loss-optical-fibre
description: Corning drew glass fibre pure enough to carry light for kilometres, turning optical communication into engineering.

name: world-series-of-poker-first
description: Benny Binion gathered leading gamblers at his Las Vegas casino for a poker tournament that crowned a world champion.

name: landsat-earth-imaging
description: A NASA satellite began imaging the land surface in repeating swaths, giving mapmakers a continuous view from orbit.

name: utc-leap-second
description: Coordinated Universal Time began inserting a spare second whenever atomic clocks ran ahead of the slowing Earth.

name: bosphorus-bridge
description: Istanbul's first suspension bridge over the Bosphorus strait carried road traffic between Europe and Asia.

name: hawking-radiation
description: Hawking showed black holes are not entirely black: quantum effects make them glow and slowly evaporate.

name: terracotta-army-discovered
description: Farmers digging a well in Shaanxi struck the head of a clay soldier, one of thousands guarding a Chinese emperor's tomb.

name: diffie-hellman-key-exchange
description: Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman showed two strangers could agree on a secret key in the open, having never met.

name: four-colour-theorem-proved
description: Appel and Haken showed four colours suffice for any map, the first major proof to lean on a computer.

name: hydrothermal-vents-discovered
description: The submersible Alvin found hot vents on the Galapagos Rift crowded with life fed by chemistry rather than sunlight.

name: rsa-algorithm-published
description: Three MIT researchers turned public-key cryptography into a working system resting on the difficulty of factoring huge numbers.

name: compact-fluorescent-lamp
description: Philips folded a fluorescent tube into a screw-in bulb, the first energy-saving lamp sold for ordinary sockets.

name: cosmic-inflation-theory
description: Guth proposed the infant universe ballooned enormously in an instant, leaving it smooth and flat.

name: sadat-assassinated
description: The Egyptian president was killed by soldiers during a military parade after making peace with Israel.

name: classification-finite-simple-groups
description: Gorenstein announced that the building blocks of finite symmetry had been listed, across thousands of pages.

name: quantum-key-distribution
description: Bennett and Brassard described sharing a key as single photons, where any eavesdropper disturbs them and is detected.

name: new-coke-launched
description: Coca-Cola replaced its original formula with a sweeter recipe, then restored the old one after a public backlash.

name: pgp-encryption-released
description: Phil Zimmermann gave away Pretty Good Privacy, putting strong encryption in ordinary hands and drawing a federal investigation.

name: ukraine-declares-independence
description: Ukraine's parliament declared independence from the Soviet Union, confirmed by an overwhelming referendum.

name: slovakia-becomes-independent
description: Czechoslovakia split peacefully in the Velvet Divorce, and Slovakia took its place as a sovereign state.

name: blue-led
description: Shuji Nakamura's gallium nitride diodes completed the colour set, making white LED lighting possible.

name: fermat-last-theorem-proved
description: Andrew Wiles closed the gap in his proof of the margin note Fermat left unproven for three and a half centuries.

name: gps-full-coverage
description: The satellite constellation was declared complete, so a receiver anywhere on Earth could fix its own position.

name: kaiko-challenger-deep
description: A Japanese remotely operated vehicle reached the deepest point of the ocean and brought back mud and amphipods.

name: rabin-assassinated
description: The Israeli prime minister was shot by an opponent of the Oslo Accords after a peace rally in Tel Aviv.

name: haart-aids-treatment
description: Triple-drug antiretroviral therapy turned HIV infection from a near-certain death sentence into a managed illness.

name: dark-energy-discovered
description: Distant supernovae revealed that cosmic expansion is speeding up, pushed by an unknown energy in space.

name: thonis-heracleion-found
description: Divers mapped the drowned Egyptian port of Thonis-Heracleion, its temples, statues and cargo ships lying under Abu Qir Bay.

name: aes-encryption-standard
description: Rijndael, a Belgian design, won an open international contest and became the cipher guarding government files and web traffic.

name: poincare-conjecture-proved
description: Grigori Perelman posted a proof that every simply connected closed three-dimensional space is a sphere.

name: darpa-grand-challenge-won
description: Stanford's driverless car Stanley crossed a desert course alone, showing autonomous driving could work.

name: google-earth-launch
description: A free virtual globe stitched satellite imagery into a zoomable model of the planet, putting survey data on home computers.

name: bhutto-assassinated
description: The former Pakistani prime minister was killed at an election rally in Rawalpindi after returning from exile.

name: chinook-solves-checkers
description: Researchers proved that perfect play at checkers ends in a draw, the largest game solved by computer to that point.

name: incandescent-bulb-phase-out
description: Australia announced a national ban on filament bulbs, and Europe and America soon legislated their own switch-off.

name: cameron-challenger-deep
description: James Cameron piloted a vertical torpedo-shaped submersible alone to the floor of the Mariana Trench.

name: richard-iii-grave-found
friendly_name: Richard III Found Under Car Park
description: Archaeologists dug up a council car park in Leicester and found the lost grave of the last Plantagenet king of England.

name: zodiac-cipher-solved
description: Three amateurs running custom software cracked the Zodiac Killer's longest cryptogram after half a century of failed attempts.

name: leap-second-retired
description: The General Conference on Weights and Measures agreed to stop adding leap seconds to civil time worldwide.

name: titan-submersible-implosion
description: A carbon-fibre tourist submersible imploded on its way down to the Titanic wreck, killing all five people aboard.
